title: canon_commit_check's remedy is inert for an attachment -- sync is not the writer, st attach is
body:
## What

`canon_commit_check.sh` refuses a commit whose canon names bytes the commit does not carry, and prints this remedy:

> Canon was written from the WORKTREE while these files were uncommitted.
> THE ORDER MATTERS AND THE OBVIOUS ONE DOES NOT WORK. Sync canon FIRST -- it reads the WORKTREE -- then commit the file(s) and canon together.

**For an ATTACHMENT that remedy cannot work, and following it changes nothing.** `intent sync --to-disk` writes the extract from the STORE; an attachment's recorded bytes are written only by `intent st attach`. **No sync direction rewrites one.** So the operator syncs, sees no change, and the guard refuses again with the same message.

## Reproduction, driven 2026-08-31

1. Edit a file that canon records as an attachment -- eg `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/fleet_corpus_conservation.sh`.
2. `intent sync --to-disk` -- reports `extract written for 69 thread(s)`, and `git status` shows **no change to `intent/.canon/st/ST0056.json`**.
3. Stage the edited file and commit. The guard refuses:
   `ADDS 1 of 1 attachment(s) examined -- the index (staged) names bytes it does not contain: ST0056/parity/tools/fleet_corpus_conservation.sh`
4. Follow the remedy exactly -- sync first, then commit. **Identical refusal.**

The fix is `intent st attach ST0056 parity/tools/fleet_corpus_conservation.sh --from <the file>`, then sync, then commit. The remedy names none of that.

## Why it matters

**A remedy that cannot work is worse than no remedy, because it spends the operator's trust before it spends their time** (vc, 2026-08-31). The refusal itself is correct and caught a real divergence; only the instruction is wrong, and it is wrong for one of the two populations the guard covers.

The guard's message is right for a GENERATED VIEW, where sync is the writer. It is wrong for an ATTACHMENT, where sync is not. **The message names no distinction, so a reader cannot tell which case they are in** -- and the attachment case is the one where the advice is not merely incomplete but inert.

This is the standing trap already recorded in this project's memory as *attachments are AUTHORED; editing a file under `intent/st/` leaves the store stale, and the canon guard's own remedy is wrong for attachments*. Filing it so it lives in the record rather than only in a node's head.

## Remedy

Branch the message on which population the offending path belongs to. If the path is a recorded attachment, name `intent st attach <ID> <PATH> --from <file>` followed by the sync; otherwise keep the current wording. The guard already knows the path is an attachment -- it says so, in the line above the remedy.

## Reach

Message only. The refusal, its narrowing to what the commit ADDS, and its gate are all correct and are not in scope here.
